pi Number(): "" -> 0ms, "  5  " -> 5ms, "0x10" -> 16ms all honored; non-finite (e.g. "abc") FALLS THROUGH to the retry-after header. ri f64 parse rejects those, and because the else-if keys on header PRESENCE, an unparseable retry-after-ms suppresses the retry-after header entirely. Scenario: response has retry-after-ms: "abc" and retry-after: "5" -> pi sleeps 5000ms; ri uses exponential backoff (1000*2^attempt) instead.
Numeric seconds * 1000, clamped at >=0 (negative -> 0), finite-check, fractional seconds supported in both.

Scenario: retry-after: "2026-07-24T12:00:00Z" -> pi computes max(0, date-now) and honors it; ri fails to parse and falls back to exponential backoff. IMF-fixdate ("Tue, 15 Nov 1994 08:12:31 GMT") and past dates (clamp to 0) behave identically.

pi: default cap 60000ms, applied ONLY to 429 retry-after values; non-429 retry-after and all exponential backoff are uncapped; maxRetryDelayMs <= 0 disables the cap. ri: no default cap (None = uncapped); when max_retry_delay_ms is set it clamps EVERY delay (exponential, retry-after on any status, network-error backoff); Some(0) clamps delays to 0. Scenarios: (a) 429 retry-after 600s, no options -> pi sleeps 60s, ri sleeps 600s; (b) 503 retry-after 120s with maxRetryDelayMs=10000 -> pi sleeps 120s (uncapped non-429), ri sleeps 10s; (c) maxRetryDelayMs=0 with 429 retry-after 5s -> pi sleeps 5s (cap disabled), ri sleeps 0ms (hot retry).
